core.p: Dickens presents [topic] as [idea], [twist], in order to [purpose for Victorian middle-class readers].

head: Topic
Thesis
rows: Scrooge

Dickens presents Scrooge as the embodiment of selfish Victorian individualism whose gradual, joyful transformation proves that even the hardest heart can change, inviting readers to recognise and reform their own attitudes.
Bob Cratchit
Bob represents the loyal, exploited working poor, whose warmth and forgiveness in poverty shame Scrooge’s coldness in wealth and challenge readers’ assumptions about the poor.
Tiny Tim
Tiny Tim turns Malthus’s ‘surplus population’ into a loved child, so that readers feel, rather than calculate, the cost of neglecting the poor.
Fred
Fred is Dickens’s mouthpiece for the Christmas spirit, whose persistent kindness shows that generosity and forgiveness, not wealth, create happiness.
The Ghosts
The Ghosts form an escalating moral education, using memory, empathy and fear to transform Scrooge, and the novella uses the same methods on its readers.
Marley
Marley is a warning made visible: his chains show that greed imprisons the soul, and his regret tells readers that ‘Mankind’ is everyone’s business.

head: Topic
Thesis
rows: Poverty
Dickens presents poverty as an injustice caused by society’s indifference, not by the moral failings of the poor, and demands that the wealthy take personal responsibility.
Redemption
Dickens shows redemption as a process of memory, empathy and fear that is always available, offering readers hope as well as a warning.
Greed vs generosity
Dickens contrasts greed, which isolates and imprisons, with generosity, which costs little but creates the true wealth of human connection.
Family and Christmas
Dickens presents Christmas as a moral season that reminds people of their bonds to family, community and the poor, values he wants kept ‘all the year’.
Time and memory
Dickens uses the past, present and future to show that memory shapes who we are but that the future is never fixed, so change is always possible.
Isolation
Dickens presents isolation as Scrooge’s self-chosen punishment, symbolised by cold, and community as the warmth that redeems him.

Scrooge’s fear of poverty (Belle: ‘You fear the world too much’)
exam.q: Write a thesis for: ‘Explain how Dickens presents the theme of fear elsewhere in the novella.’
exam.tip: Look for two kinds of the theme to make your thesis conceptual.

mistakes.r: Add Dickens’s purpose and an interpretive twist.

summary: A bank of grade 9 thesis statements for every likely A Christmas Carol topic; each links an idea to Dickens’s purpose for his Victorian readers and can be adapted in the first minutes of the exam.

terms.d: A short argument that answers the question for the whole text.
